unitType.label: Unit type
unitType.host: Dedicated GPU host (Linux, nvidia-smi, not a Spark)
unitType.windows: Windows PC (NVIDIA GPU or AMD Strix Halo)

addSpark.title: Add Spark/GPU Host
addSpark.localHost: This host (local collectors, no SSH for metrics)
addSpark.localHostEdit: This host (local collectors — no SSH for metrics)
addSpark.windowsHelp: Needs the Windows OpenSSH Server and the NVIDIA driver (nvidia-smi). Metrics come from PowerShell over SSH; Hermes and Tailnet checks are not available for Windows.
addSpark.localNoIpHost: Local metrics still work. Open links and directed Wake-on-LAN need a LAN IP.
addSpark.localNoIpSpark: Local metrics still work. Open links need a LAN IP. DGX Spark has no Wake-on-LAN.
addSpark.sshPortHelp: Default port 22. Change it when sshd listens elsewhere.
addSpark.sshPortHelpEdit: Default 22. Use this when sshd listens elsewhere.
addSpark.sshKeyHelp: SSH runs on the sparkDash host (not your browser). In Docker, mount a private key at /root/.ssh/id_ed25519 (see docker-compose.yml) or set SSH_IDENTITY_FILE. IPs are from that host's network. Mark this machine as “This host” so it skips SSH.
addSpark.sshPasswordHelp: Stored encrypted on the server (not in sparks.json, not returned by the API). Survives Docker restarts.
addSpark.passwordRequired: Password is required when SSH auth is Password
addSpark.testHelp: Checks SSH, hardware and LLM before you add it. Optional.
addSpark.name: Name (required)
addSpark.nameHelp: Shown in the sidebar and on the Overview.
addSpark.workerNoPorts: Workers have no local LLM API, so no ports are probed.
addSpark.comfyHelp: Job queue and live progress. Default port 8188.
addSpark.hermesHelp: Checks for new releases every 10 min and adds an Update Hermes button.

editSpark.name: Name
editSpark.macUsing: Using enP7s7 automatically ({{mac}}). Leave blank to keep auto, or enter a different MAC.
editSpark.macBlank: Leave blank to use enP7s7 once the host has been online and detected.
editSpark.roleHelpTitle: Head always monitors the local LLM. Standalone can opt in/out. Workers have no local API — the LLM card is hidden and ports are not probed.
editSpark.roleHelpAria: Head always monitors the local LLM. Standalone can opt in or out. Workers hide the LLM card and do not probe ports.
editSpark.llmMonitoringTitle: When enabled, probe the local LLM API and show the LLM card on this Spark.
editSpark.llmMonitoringAria: Enable probing the local LLM API and showing the LLM card.
editSpark.comfyMonitoringTitle: When enabled, probe ComfyUI on this host and show a ComfyUI card. Default port is 8188 — change the port value on the right if needed.
editSpark.comfyMonitoringAria: Enable probing ComfyUI and showing the ComfyUI card.
editSpark.hermesTitle: Hermes Agent CLI is installed on this machine (nousresearch/hermes-agent). When enabled, sparkDash checks for updates (hermes update --check) and can run “hermes update” for you via SSH with one click.
editSpark.hermesAria: Hermes Agent CLI is installed on this machine; enable update monitoring and one-click updates.
editSpark.hermesHelp: Checks for updates in the background (10 min) and adds an "Update Hermes" button that runs hermes update on this machine via SSH.
editSpark.tailnetTitle: When enabled, run `tailscale status --json` on this host and show a Tailnet card. Catches a unit that is healthy on the LAN but has fallen off its tailnet. Requires the tailscale CLI. Default off.
editSpark.tailnetAria: Enable reporting this unit's tailnet presence.
editSpark.workerLabelHelp: Shown on the overview card. Leave blank to show “distributed”.
editSpark.headHelp: Optional. Which Spark serves as the cluster head for this worker.
editSpark.passwordRequiredHint: (required — saved even if host is offline)
editSpark.passwordStored: Password is stored encrypted on this server. Offline Sparks still keep it and reconnect automatically when back up.
editSpark.passwordEnterOnce: Enter once and Save (or Test). Stored encrypted — host does not need to be online.
editSpark.passwordSavedEncrypted: Password saved encrypted (works even while host is offline).
editSpark.enterPasswordFirst: Enter the SSH password first — it will be saved even if the host is down.
editSpark.passwordRequiredForAuth: Password required for password-auth Sparks (saved encrypted, host can be offline).

harness.title: Harness sessions
harness.name: Name
harness.newToken: New bearer token (leave blank to keep the saved one)
harness.routesHelp: A route sends one harness to a Spark and port. A directory prefix wins over a general route. Rows with no route stay off the cards.
harness.urlInvalidProtocol: Use an http or https URL
harness.urlHasCredentials: Remove the username and password from the URL
harness.portRange: Each route needs a port from 1 to 65535

alerts.title: Alert notifications
alerts.sendNotificationsHelp: The server watches the Health findings and the Overview exceptions and notifies the channels below when one holds for its wait, and again when it clears. Off by default: while off nothing is evaluated or sent. Saved immediately.
alerts.offNote: Turn notifications on to change what notifies and where.
alerts.sourceStripHelp: The conditions the Overview exceptions strip shows.
alerts.sourceHealthHelp: The findings on the unit cards, with the Health rules' own thresholds.
alerts.waitMustBeNumber: {{name}}: the wait must be a number of seconds
alerts.channelsHelp: URLs are stored encrypted with the unit passwords and shown masked. They may point at the LAN (a self-hosted ntfy) or the internet, under the same rules as unit and LLM addresses; redirects are not followed.
alerts.noChannels: No channels yet: alerts still show on the Overview strip.
alerts.urlHidden: Stored URL is hidden. Leave it to keep it, or paste a new one.
alerts.urlMissing: No URL is stored for this channel. Enter it again.
alerts.remindHelp: Repeat the notification for an alert that has not cleared.
alerts.recentHelp: Fired and cleared since the server started. Every notification sent or failed is also on the Activity page.

gpuClock.readFailed: Could not read the GPU clock cap
gpuClock.bootFailed: The @reboot job ran at this boot and could not re-apply the cap, so the GPU is not capped. Press Apply to cap it again, or check that sudo -n nvidia-smi -lgc still works for this user.
gpuClock.confirmKeep: Keep the cap after reboot with {{how}}? It re-applies the cap at every boot on this unit.
gpuClock.cappedKeptCron: Capped at {{mhz}} MHz and kept after reboot by an @reboot cron job.
gpuClock.cappedKeptService: Capped at {{mhz}} MHz and kept after reboot by a boot service.
gpuClock.cappedUntilReboot: Capped at {{mhz}} MHz until the next reboot.
gpuClock.removeConfirm: Remove the GPU clock cap and its boot hook from this unit?
gpuClock.commandApplyTitlePersist: Cap at {{mhz}} MHz and keep after reboot
gpuClock.sudoPasswordHelp: This unit has no passwordless sudo. The password is sent once, over this connection, to run the change, then discarded: it is never stored or logged.
gpuClock.insecureHelp: This connection is not on https or the machine itself, so a sudo password is not typed here (it would cross the network in the clear). Open the dashboard over https or from the Spark itself, run the change on the Spark with the command below, or give that user passwordless sudo for nvidia-smi -lgc and -rgc — a rule for those two commands is enough.
gpuClock.runsCommand: Runs nvidia-smi -lgc 0,MAX through sudo, using the saved connection settings. Applies at once; it is not part of Save.
gpuClock.runsCommandRoot: Runs nvidia-smi -lgc 0,MAX as root on this machine, using the saved connection settings. Applies at once; it is not part of Save.
gpuClock.cannotPersist: Keeping the cap after reboot needs either passwordless sudo for a root shell (the boot service) or a running cron service (an @reboot job), and this unit offers neither. The cap applies until the next reboot.
gpuClock.invalidRangeMax: Enter a whole number from {{min}} to {{max}}.
gpuClock.manualSummary: Run it on the Spark yourself
gpuClock.manualHelp: Paste the command into a terminal on the Spark. It uses plain sudo, so it asks for your password there. It is the same steps the Apply and Remove buttons run.
gpuClock.commandAria: Command to run on the Spark

fleetClock.unknown: No unit reports its clock right now — reopen Settings to try again.
fleetClock.nowCappedOne: Now: capped at {{mhz}} MHz on {{count}} unit
fleetClock.nowCappedMany: Now: capped at {{mhz}} MHz on {{count}} units
fleetClock.keepAfterReboot: Keep after reboot — the state you pick also installs a boot hook on each unit
fleetClock.noHook: Not offered here: these units have no boot hook the cap can use — neither a root shell for the boot service nor a running cron service for an @reboot job. The cap applies until the next reboot.
fleetClock.pendingHint: Not applied yet — press Save to change every unit.
fleetClock.msgNoUnit: No unit completed the requested change — some changes may have applied
fleetClock.keptCron: — kept by an @reboot cron job on each unit
fleetClock.keptMixed: — kept after reboot (boot service or @reboot job, per unit)
fleetClock.untickHint: Untick “Keep after reboot” to cap until the next reboot instead.

network.sensorsUnavailable: Sensor readings unavailable; last health sample {{age}}.
network.liveUnknown: Live port readings are unknown. Cached values are not shown as current traffic.
network.tableCaption: Fabric ports; RX and TX are from the switch perspective
network.retention: {{days}}-day retention. Collection starts when monitoring is enabled; earlier history is not reconstructed. RX and TX have independent full-duplex utilisation. Where SNMP does not report speed, utilisation uses the labelled configured bandwidth.
network.historyFailed: History unavailable. Retry automatically in 30 seconds.
network.trafficNote: Traffic: highest {{sample}}s sampled rate per {{bucket}} bucket. Short bursts are preserved; this is not the bucket average. Temperatures are point samples.
